Two linked, practical courses for biologists who want to analyse their own data in **R** — built around real pathogen-genomics and biology examples, with worked exercises and full solutions.

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### 🧬 [R for Bioinformatics](r-for-bioinformatics/index.qmd)
From "I can open RStudio" to building documented, tested, installable tools.

**5 parts · 17 modules** — the R mindset, files & objects, the tidyverse, Bioconductor, and writing your own package.

[Start the R course →](r-for-bioinformatics/index.qmd)
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### 📊 [Statistics for Biologists](statistics-for-biologists/index.qmd)
From study design to generalised and mixed models — correctly and reproducibly.

**6 parts · 16 modules** — description, probability, hypothesis testing, linear models, GLMs & mixed models, multivariate methods.

[Start the Stats course →](statistics-for-biologists/index.qmd) · [Which test should I use?](statistics-for-biologists/choosing-a-test.qmd)
:::

:::

## How to use these courses

Each part has **theory** pages and an **exercises** page (with downloadable `.R` scripts and full solutions). Work the theory and exercises together, in order; open the solutions only after trying.

The courses assume you can install R and RStudio. The Statistics course assumes the basic R taught in the R course. All example data is in the `data/` folder of the [repository](https://github.com/USERNAME/bio-courses) — replace `USERNAME` with your GitHub account.
